summary: Halyard mutual NDA matches the playbook throughout; counterparty edits are mostly spelling, but they add independent contractors to Representatives, request a 2-year survival period and request a Delaware or New York governing law.

findings.quote: [[INS: VERIDIAN CLOUD, INC.]]
findings.why: The counterparty entity details were filled in and the company number deleted, so the entity needs checking against the register; this is a known entity-details request rather than a playbook rule.
findings.draft_redline: Accept the entity details once the lawyer confirms Veridian Cloud, Inc. against the Delaware register.
findings.note_to_counterparty: Thank you for completing your entity details; we will confirm them against the company register and revert if anything needs correcting.

findings.quote: the Receiving Party undertakes to the Disclosing Party that it shall:
findings.why: Obligations are framed by Disclosing Party and Receiving Party roles that either Party can hold, so the NDA is genuinely mutual.

findings.quote: either marked or identified as confidential at the time of disclosure or would reasonably be considered confidential
findings.why: The definition covers information disclosed for the Purpose that is marked or reasonably confidential and includes derived notes and analyses.

findings.quote: not use or exploit the Disclosing Party's Confidential Information in any way except solely for the Purpose
findings.why: Use is limited solely to the Purpose, which is discussions on a potential commercial relationship.

findings.quote: can demonstrate by written records or other reasonable evidence
findings.why: All four carve-outs (public domain, already held, third-party receipt, independent development) are present and unnarrowed, with an accepted evidence standard.

findings.quote: [[INS: independent contractors,]]
findings.why: The counterparty added independent contractors to Representatives, widening permitted disclosure beyond the playbook's list of employees, officers, directors, advisers, auditors, insurers and Group members.
findings.draft_redline: Delete "independent contractors," from the definition of Representatives, or limit it to contractors bound by written confidentiality obligations no less onerous than this Agreement and who strictly need to know.
findings.note_to_counterparty: We would prefer not to extend Representatives to independent contractors as this widens the circle of recipients; we could consider it if such contractors are bound by written confidentiality obligations and you remain liable for them.

findings.quote: those of its Representatives and members of its Group who strictly need to know such Confidential Information
findings.why: Disclosure to Representatives and Group members is allowed on a need-to-know basis and the Receiving Party stays liable for them under 4.1.3.

findings.quote: to the extent that it is legally permitted to do so:
findings.why: Compelled disclosure is permitted, notice and cooperation apply only where legally permitted, and resisting disclosure is at the Disclosing Party's cost.

findings.quote: within ten Business Days of receipt of such request:
findings.why: Return or destruction within ten Business Days with officer-signed confirmation, and 6.2 and 6.3 keep the backup and legally required copy exceptions with continuing confidentiality.

findings.quote: [[INS: or a federal holiday in the United States]]
findings.why: The extra US holiday and San Francisco bank days only slightly extend the Business Day period for return, which stays well above 5 Business Days.
findings.fallback_cited: Any period of 5 Business Days or more.

findings.quote: other than the limited right to use the Confidential Information solely for the Purpose
findings.why: Ownership and IP stay with the Disclosing Party under 7.1 and no licence is granted beyond use for the Purpose.

findings.quote: All Confidential Information is provided by the Disclosing Party on an "as is" basis.
findings.why: Information is as is with no warranty, reliance liability is excluded save for fraud, and there is no obligation to proceed (7.4, 7.5).

findings.quote: without the prior written consent of the other Party, except as required by law
findings.why: Mutual publicity restriction requiring prior written consent, with a legal-requirement exception.

findings.quote: that Party shall not disclose such personal data unless and until the Parties have agreed and entered into a separate written data processing agreement
findings.why: Only business contact details are anticipated and any other personal data requires a separate DPA first.

findings.quote: for a period of two (2) years, unless terminated earlier by either Party giving not less than thirty (30) days' prior written notice
findings.why: Two-year term with 30 days' notice to terminate early, as preferred.

findings.quote: Would Halyard be open to reducing this from 3 years to 2 years?
findings.why: The counterparty asks to cut general survival from 3 to 2 years while keeping Trade Secrets protected as long as they qualify, which is within the accepted 2 to 5 year range.

findings.quote: a Party shall be entitled to seek the remedies of injunction, specific performance and other equitable relief
findings.why: Equitable relief is mutual, framed as entitled to seek, and 11.2 makes remedies cumulative.

findings.quote: without the prior written consent of the other Party.
findings.why: Neither Party may assign or deal with its rights without the other's prior written consent.

findings.quote: not reverse engineer, decompile, disassemble or otherwise attempt to derive the composition, source code or underlying structure
findings.why: Reverse engineering of software and prototypes is prohibited.

findings.quote: [[INS: (such as DocuSign or Adobe Sign)]]
findings.why: The insertion only gives examples of electronic signature platforms in the existing counterparts and e-signature clause.
findings.fallback_cited: Any customary drafting, including archaic wording of standard positions.

findings.quote: our strong preference is to govern this NDA under the laws of the State of Delaware or the State of New York
findings.why: The counterparty asks for Delaware or New York law, or silence on law and venue, instead of English law.
findings.draft_redline: This Agreement and any dispute or claim arising out of or in connection with it shall be governed by the law of England and Wales, and the courts of England and Wales shall have non-exclusive jurisdiction.
findings.note_to_counterparty: We are unable to agree to Delaware or New York law, but we can offer English law with non-exclusive jurisdiction of the English courts so that you are not tied to one forum.

findings.quote: the courts of England and Wales shall have exclusive jurisdiction
findings.why: The clause as drafted provides exclusive jurisdiction of the courts of England and Wales, as preferred.
